affect the interface with Wireshark, i.e. stdout and return value.

Add documentation in Users Guide about this command line tool.

Closes #20520

Like the comment above says, could we convert to using ws_getopt_long() since the options are getting more complicated?
Yes, I've read this, and opted not use it and pull in everything related to it.

Is that a "don't want to do the work (but okay if someone else does it)" or you're just opposed to "adding that much dependency for such a small app"? (is mmdbresolve not already linking to wsutil?)

I'm for the "standardization of code for all apps in the repo" as my argument for why getopt should be used if you're deciding to change/add this functionality.

Aren't there some license issues with libmaxminddb being Apache 2.0 licensed, which isn't quite compatible with GPLv2, which is part of the whole reason that mmmdbresolve is a separate, MIT licensed program that only includes system headers?
That would be a reason to avoid including and linking with all sorts of other files in the repo.

If I recall a discussion with a lawyer correctly[1], the GPL-2.0-or-later and Apache-2.0 licenses aren't compatible. The the GPL-3.0-or-later and Apache-2.0 licenses *are* compatible, so linking with wsutil would trigger the "or any later version" clause in wsutil's license and make mmdbresolve available under the GPLv3-or-later. GLib is available under the LGPL-2.1-or-later license, so as long as we complied with section 5 and be a "work that uses the Library" there wouldn't be any license version trigger.

[1] The discussion was about the Falco Bridge plugin and falcodump, which link with libscap and libsinsp, which are Apache-2.0. I'm pretty sure this means Stratoshark is GPLv3-or-later.
I'm OK with the MR as it currently stands. I'd be OK with GOption as well.
Didn't realize "licensing" was the real issue, I was just trying to get consistent code across applications.
